 Knocked Loose, Angine de Poitrine, Hayley Williams and Mastodon among rock and metal GRAMMY nominees
 The GRAMMYs are unveiling their nominations today, and there's plenty of rock representation, including an impressive four nods for Angine de Poitrine.
 November 16, 2026
 Words: 
 Emma Wilkes
 Photo: 
 Jared Leibowitz
 The GRAMMY nominations for 2027 are being rolled out, and it looks like there’ll be a fierce contest for this year’s prizes in the rock and metal categories. 
 Angine de Poitrine have picked up four nods in total, including for the Rock Performance and Alternative Music Performance categories, as well as for Best Rock Album. They've also got a nomination for one of the GRAMMYs' biggest categories, Best New Artist, which for an artist of their size and sound is pretty damn massive. 
 Knocked Loose have also earned their second nomination, following their nod in 2025 for Best Metal Performance with Suffocate. They’re up for the same category with their Denzel Curry collab Hive Mind, duking it out against Megadeth, Mastodon, Anthrax and Amy Lee’s mega-collab with Poppy and Courtney LaPlante, End Of You. 
 There’s also been nominations for Hayley Williams, Foo Fighters and Muse. 
 Check it out below:
 Best Rock Performance 
 Angine de Poitrine - Sarniezz
Phoebe Bridgers - Lost Boys
Geese - Trinidad
Olivia Rodrigo ft. Robert Smith - what’s wrong with me?
The Rolling Stones - In The Stars
 Best Metal Performance 
 Anthrax - The Edge of Perfection
Knocked Loose ft. Denzel Curry - Hive Mind
Mastodon - Your Ghost Again
Megadeth - Let There Be Shred
Amy Lee, Poppy & Courtney LaPlante - End Of You 
 Best Alternative Music Performance 
 Angine de Poitrine - Fabienk
Phoebe Bridgers - Kill Me
Geese - Au Pays du Cocaine
Rosalia - Reliquia
Hayley Williams - Showbiz
 Best Rock Album 
 Angine de Poitrine - Vol. II
Foo Fighters - Your Favorite Toy
Muse - The Wow! Signal
The Rolling Stones - Foreign Tongues
Jack White - Frozen Charlotte
 Best Rock Song 
 The Rolling Stones - In The Stars
Phoebe Bridgers - Lost Boys
Aerosmith & Yungblud - My Only Angel
Bruce Springsteen - Streets of Minneapolis (Radio Mix)
Geese - Trinidad
Olivia Rodrigo ft. Robert Smith - what’s wrong with me?
 Talking of the GRAMMYs, there's a big congratulations due for The Warning, who won a Latin GRAMMY over the weekend for their song Ego. 
 The ceremony for the 2027 GRAMMYs will take place on February 7 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.
